subject: Capacity catch-up, credits & rollover options
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@bluewave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Usage spike — request for catch-up discussion

Hi Irene,

We noticed a significant backdated usage spike on our account for October that resulted in a one-time overage charge on our November bill. This spike was driven by an event we ran on Oct 18–20 (unplanned burst traffic to an API flow).

Can we schedule a quick call this week to review the hourly breakdown and discuss options for smoothing the charge? Ideally we want to avoid a hard surprise to our finance team, and are open to a blended credit, spreading the cost, or moving to a committed/dedicated configuration to prevent a recurrence.

Attaching an exported usage report for the period — it's hourly and shows the Oct 18 spike.

Attachments: usage_report_nov_spike_hourly.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Director, Infrastructure & Analytics
BlueWave Analytics
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@bluewave.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike — request for catch-up discussion

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and the CSV. I’m sorry this landed as a surprise. We track hourly utilization but the burst on Oct 18 looks atypical given your baseline.

I’ll loop in Rohan (account) and Monica (billing ops) to dig into the invoice and see whether the spike aligns with our internal attribution windows (ingest vs scheduled jobs). Two asks from my side to speed things up:
- Can you confirm whether any non-prod keys were used for the event?
- If you have a PO number or renewal excerpt that references committed capacity, please send it over (helps with eligibility for credits).

We’ll aim to send a proposed remediation (credit vs amortized charge vs plan change) within 10 business days. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow at 11am PT if that works for you.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@bluewave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: 2026-11-05T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike — request for catch-up discussion

Thanks, Irene — 11am PT tomorrow works.

Answers to your questions:
- No non-prod keys were used; this was production traffic from a short-lived campaign.
- We renewed in April; attaching the contract excerpt showing the committed baseline.

Also attaching an hourly CSV that breaks out traffic by model and region — the majority of the spike is on the text-generation route.

Attachments: contract-excerpt-q2-renewal.pdf (PDF, 90 KB); usage_report_nov_spike_hourly.csv (CSV, updated)

Sara
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@bluewave.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed catch-up: credit + transition option

Hi Sara — following our call and after reviewing the attached usage and contract excerpt, here’s what we can propose to resolve the one-time overage without creating billing friction for BlueWave: 

1) One-time catch-up credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 35% of the overage line-item. This reflects partial waiving in recognition of the event being a short spike and our interest in keeping you on a stable path.

2) Rollover / committed option: As an alternative, we can convert the overage amount into a 3-month amortized charge that buys committed Dedicated capacity equal to the peak baseline. This includes a credit equal to 50% of the overage applied toward the committed pool, and unused committed capacity can roll forward (monthly rollover up to 2 months).

3) Operational guardrails: To prevent recurrence we’ll enable a safety throttle for the affected route and add a weekly usage digest for your infra team for the next 60 days.

I’ve attached a draft invoice showing both options side-by-side and a mutual action plan that documents acceptance steps, PO/invoice routing, and timing. If you prefer the credit route we’ll issue a credit memo on your account and apply it to next month’s invoice; if you choose the committed route we’ll issue a single invoice for the amortized commitment and ship a revised subscription amendment.

Attachments: draft-invoice-BWA-20261115.pdf; mutual-action-plan-BWA.docx

Thoughts? If acceptable I can route for approval and procurement invoicing — what timeline does BlueWave need for the invoice/PO?

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@bluewave.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: 2026-11-21T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed catch-up: credit + transition option

Rohan / Irene — thanks for the clear options and the MAP. We discussed with finance and procurement and would like to proceed with Option 1 (one-time credit of 35% applied as a credit memo). A couple of operational notes:

- Please send the credit memo and revised invoice to procurement@bluewave.com and include our PO# BW-2026-7788 on the invoice.
- We’ll take you up on the weekly digest for 60 days; please start the digest the week of Nov 29.
- Can you confirm the credit posting timeline? We need it reflected on our Dec 1 close.

If you can confirm next steps (who will issue the credit memo, expected posting date), we’ll route the PO on our side immediately.

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic approach.

Sara Liu
Director, Infrastructure & Analytics
BlueWave Analytics

Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sara — we’ll process this. I’ll have Monica coordinate the credit memo and final invoice routing.
>
> Irene
> Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
> Redwood Inference
